findings.title: Go and Python disagree on required nonempty report fields; invalid reports can approve and clear BLOCK
findings.diagnosis: internal/host/report_contract.go:22 uses strings.TrimSpace. Python validate_report.py uses str.strip, which additionally treats U+001C through U+001F as whitespace. A current, receipt-bound pass report with audit_id, target, requirement id and evidence reference consisting only of each such character fails the authoritative Python validator but has no Go violations. review-import records APPROVE; findings-import removes PRIOR/BLOCK; requireHostTransitionGate returns nil. This satisfies the host gate only; no actual stage transition or human approval was fabricated.

evidence.observation: Four subcases reproduce Python exit 1, Go violations=[], APPROVE, empty findings, and gate=<nil>.
The nonempty predicate is reused across contract fields. Its false acceptance feeds the approval map and approving findings replacement.
Retained exact invalid report plus host/core records show the prior BLOCK and its replacement.

fix.action: In internal/host/report_contract.go, use one nonempty predicate with the authoritative Python strip whitespace set, including U+001C..U+001F. Extend parity tests across all nonempty fields and route approval tests through each invalid report. Keep invalid reports ESCALATE or refused, and preserve blockers.
fix.why: The imported report contract must have the same field semantics in Go and Python before pass can authorize an approving snapshot.

verification.method: Run auditor TestAuditorReportWhitespaceParity for U+001C..U+001F, with the existing valid current report control.
verification.expected: Every Python-invalid report refuses or escalates, retains PRIOR/BLOCK, and leaves the host gate closed. Valid current report still approves.

verification.method: Differentially test nonempty fields using ASCII whitespace, U+0085, U+00A0, U+2007, U+202F, the four controls, and mixed real text.
verification.expected: Go and Python accept and reject the same inputs.

fix.tradeoffs: A report with previously accepted control-only fields will no longer approve. This is a small compatibility restriction on invalid reports. No schema or stage semantics need to change.
fix.alternative: Call the canonical Python validator before approval. This avoids the port gap but adds a runtime dependency to the standalone Go integration.

findings.title: Interrupted output-artifact writes are trusted as complete on retry
findings.diagnosis: retainOutput creates the final digest-named path with O_EXCL before writing bytes. An interrupted process can leave that final path empty or partial. On retry, os.ErrExist returns its reference without reading or validating it. An auditor fixture places an empty file at the exact expected path, representing a crash between OpenFile and Write. loop-evidence then reports EVIDENCE_RECORDED and appends both records with a reference to 0 bytes instead of the required 99-byte output artifact. No same-UID adversary is needed for this failure state. The test simulates crash residue; it does not claim to have killed a process at that instruction.

evidence.observation: loop-evidence accepts with exit 0; output_ref resolves to 0 bytes, expected 99; OutputDigest=c7d386429b24fec97b446d8e2b50a23942057ca5ab8b8a9839776f0ca443fd16 cannot be reconstructed from that artifact.
The final name is created before Write/Sync, and the existing-file branch returns without validating content.

fix.action: In retainOutput, validate the exact bytes/digest and regular-file type of an existing artifact before returning a reference. Publish new artifacts only after a complete temporary file is written and synced, with atomic no-clobber publication and directory sync. Refuse a corrupt existing artifact before either evidence append; preserve it for diagnosis.
fix.why: A final digest-named path must identify complete bytes, including after interruption. Filename existence alone does not prove content integrity.

verification.method: Run TestAuditorOutputInterruptedArtifact with empty, truncated and wrong-byte existing artifacts, plus a valid existing-artifact control.
verification.expected: Incomplete/corrupt artifacts never produce accepted evidence. Valid existing artifacts reproduce both streams and OutputDigest.

verification.method: Interrupt artifact publication before and after sync/publish, restart and repeat capture.
verification.expected: Every accepted output_ref is complete and verifiable. No partial final artifact is trusted; both chains remain unchanged on corrupt-artifact refusal.

fix.tradeoffs: Existing-artifact reuse adds a bounded read/hash. Atomic no-clobber publication needs platform-aware handling. Recovery must not silently rewrite evidence history.
fix.alternative: Keep exclusive final-path writes but validate existing bytes and fail closed on mismatch; this contains false evidence while leaving manual recovery for crash residue.

limitations: Fresh audit context contains original objective, approved source sections and the sanitized closure criteria only. The required v7 source header contains a historical Gate A verdict; source artifacts and comments naturally contain author claims. No prior Gate C verdict or implementer conversation was read before Phase 1. This is context isolation, not an OS-enforced read-only mount or proof of hidden system routing.

All execution used a copied repository or Go overlays under this output directory. Audit permissions, rather than an OS-enforced read-only filesystem, protected the original repository. No target edits, Git mutations on the target, nested agent CLIs or model APIs were used. Existing tests create and mutate synthetic Git fixtures outside the target.

Fixtures use synthetic receipts, route approvals and host preflight telemetry. No live worker, exact-route hi, authentic human stage transition, or final outcome closure was executed. This is the Gate C integration audit, not Gate F real-worker dogfood.

Gate D reservations, leases/generations, independent criterion credit, reproduced kernel/budget dispositions and full contract-dependent packet inputs are excluded by explicit human decision. Their exit tests remain required before later claims.

The first full normal/race suites failed one unchanged dogfood-helper test because the repository copy was under os.TempDir. Both complete suites passed after giving tests a separate TMPDIR; both initial logs remain available.

Independent probes reuse repository fixture setup helpers but define their own test inputs, adverse cases and assertions. Tests are finite; passed suites are not proof over all possible concurrency schedules or filesystems.
Crash residue was simulated at the artifact filename boundary. No real power loss or storage-failure injection was performed.
No approved Jev tool is exposed. Auditor decisions use the permitted fallback; no model/API substitution was made.
